To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the choice of the intravenously infused volume expander influences the tolerance of progressive anemia in an anesthetized porcine model of acute hemorrhage, and that third-generation tetrastarchs (e.g., 6% HES with a molar mass of 130 kDa and a degree of hydroxyethyl substitution of 0.4) may have a beneficial impact on the maintenance and preservation of tissue oxygenation in this setting.
the choice of the intravascular fluid influences the tolerance and the maintenance of oxygen supply during acute normo-volemic anemia.
the use of tetrastarch solutions in anemic patients may improve oxygen delivery to tissues, as compared to the use of other crystalloid or colloid solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel concept of acute anemic normovolemia.
the development and evaluation of new methods for the treatment of patients suffering from acute blood loss.
the question, whether the choice of the intravascular volume replacement fluid influences the tolerance to acute normovolemia in anesthetised pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of HES 130 is associated with a better oxygen supply during hemodilution than HES 450 and gelatin.
the choice of the intravenious fluid has an impact of the tolerance of acute anemia.
the choice of the intravascular volume substitution fluid influences the tolerance to acute normovolaemic anemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of tetrastarch 6% HES (130/0.40) is superior compared with the use of gelatine, Ringer's solution and HES 6% (450/0.70) regarding maintenance of tissue perfusion and oxygenation during acute normovolemia induced by hemodilution.
HES 130 is superior to Ringer's solution, gelatin and 6% HES in the setting of acute normovolemia induced anemia.
the choice of the intravascular fluid has an impact in maintaining tissue oxygenation during acute normovolemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of intravenous fluid influences tolerance of acute normo-volemic anemia.
the use of a tetrastarch with a low molecular weight and low degree of substitution (e.g., 6% HES130/0.40) is advantageous for maintaining tissue oxygenation in anemia induced by volume replacement.
the choice of the intravenious fluid influences the tolerance to acute anemia in an animal model.
